q-102452.name: Question 1
q-102452.problem:
Find ${f}^{″}(2,1)$ for the function $f(x,y)$ given that
${f}^{′}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}-2xy & 2y-{x}^{2}\end{aligned}]$
q-102452.worked_solution:
For a function $f:{R}^{n}\to R,$ given by

$$
f:{{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}⟶f({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}),
$$

the second derivative of $f$ is given by the $n\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{″}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}^{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have

$$
{f}^{″}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

First, notice that since ${f}^{′}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}-2xy & 2y-{x}^{2}\end{aligned}],$ 
 we must have

$$
\frac{∂f}{∂x}=-2xy,\,\frac{∂f}{∂y}=2y-{x}^{2}.
$$

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(-2xy)=-2y\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2y-{x}^{2})=-2x \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(-2xy)=-2x\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(2y-{x}^{2})=2\end{aligned}
$$

So, the second derivative is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}-2y & -2x \\ -2x & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate this matrix at $(2,1).$ This gives

$$
{f}^{″}(2,1)=[\begin{aligned}-2 & -4 \\ -4 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

EXPLANATION

For a function f:Rn→R, given by f:[x1x2⋮xn]⏟x⟶f(x1,x2,…,xn),

the second derivative of f is given by the n×n matrix

f″(x)=[∂2f∂x12∂2f∂x1∂x2⋯∂2f∂x1∂xn∂2f∂x2∂x1∂2f∂x22⋯∂2f∂x2∂xn⋮⋮⋮⋮∂2f∂xn∂x1∂2f∂xn∂x2⋯∂2f∂xn2].

In our case, we have

f″(x,y)=[∂2f∂x2∂2f∂x∂y∂2f∂y∂x∂2f∂y2].

First, notice that since f′(x,y)=[−2xy2y−x2], we must have ∂f∂x=−2xy,∂f∂y=2y−x2.

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

∂2f∂x2=∂∂x(−2xy)=−2y∂2f∂x∂y=∂∂x(2y−x2)=−2x∂2f∂y∂x=∂∂y(−2xy)=−2x∂2f∂y2=∂∂y(2y−x2)=2

So, the second derivative is

f″(x,y)=[−2y−2x−2x2].

Finally, we evaluate this matrix at (2,1). This gives

f″(2,1)=[−2−4−42].

q-80940.name: Question 2
q-80940.problem:
Find ${f}^{″}(x,y)$ for the function $f(x,y)$ given that
${f}^{′}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}3{x}^{2}-y & -x\end{aligned}]$
q-80940.worked_solution:
For a function $f:{R}^{n}\to R,$ given by

$$
f:{{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}⟶f({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}),
$$

the second derivative of $f$ is given by the $n\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{″}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}^{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have

$$
{f}^{″}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

First, notice that since ${f}^{′}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}3{x}^{2}-y & -x\end{aligned}],$ we must have

$$
\frac{∂f}{∂x}=3{x}^{2}-y,\,\frac{∂f}{∂y}=-x.
$$

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(3{x}^{2}-y)=6x\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(-x)=-1 \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(3{x}^{2}-y)=-1\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(-x)=0\end{aligned}
$$

So, the second derivative is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}6x & -1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Find f″(x,y) for the function f(x,y) given that f′(x,y)=[3x2−y−x]

a
[3x2−y−x−x0]
b
[6x−x−x0]
c
[3x200−x]
d
[3x2−y−1−1−x]
e
[6x−1−10]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

For a function f:Rn→R, given by f:[x1x2⋮xn]⏟x⟶f(x1,x2,…,xn),

the second derivative of f is given by the n×n matrix

f″(x)=[∂2f∂x12∂2f∂x1∂x2⋯∂2f∂x1∂xn∂2f∂x2∂x1∂2f∂x22⋯∂2f∂x2∂xn⋮⋮⋮⋮∂2f∂xn∂x1∂2f∂xn∂x2⋯∂2f∂xn2].

In our case, we have

f″(x,y)=[∂2f∂x2∂2f∂x∂y∂2f∂y∂x∂2f∂y2].

First, notice that since f′(x,y)=[3x2−y−x], we must have

∂f∂x=3x2−y,∂f∂y=−x.

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

∂2f∂x2=∂∂x(3x2−y)=6x∂2f∂x∂y=∂∂x(−x)=−1∂2f∂y∂x=∂∂y(3x2−y)=−1∂2f∂y2=∂∂y(−x)=0

So, the second derivative is

f″(x,y)=[6x−1−10].

q-102477.name: Question 3
q-102477.problem:
Find ${f}^{″}(1,2)$ for the function $f(x,y)$ given that
${f}^{′}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}y-2xy & x-{x}^{2}\end{aligned}]$
q-102477.worked_solution:
For a function $f:{R}^{n}\to R,$ given by

$$
f:{{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}⟶f({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}),
$$

the second derivative of $f$ is given by the $n\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{″}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}^{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have

$$
{f}^{″}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

First, notice that since ${f}^{′}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}y-2xy & x-{x}^{2}\end{aligned}],$ 
 we must have

$$
\frac{∂f}{∂x}=y-2xy,\,\frac{∂f}{∂y}=x-{x}^{2}.
$$

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(y-2xy)=-2y\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(x-{x}^{2})=1-2x \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(y-2xy)=1-2x\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(x-{x}^{2})=0\end{aligned}
$$

So, the second derivative is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}-2y & 1-2x \\ 1-2x & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate this matrix at $(1,2).$ This gives

$$
{f}^{″}(1,2)=[\begin{aligned}-4 & -1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

EXPLANATION

For a function f:Rn→R, given by f:[x1x2⋮xn]⏟x⟶f(x1,x2,…,xn),

the second derivative of f is given by the n×n matrix

f″(x)=[∂2f∂x12∂2f∂x1∂x2⋯∂2f∂x1∂xn∂2f∂x2∂x1∂2f∂x22⋯∂2f∂x2∂xn⋮⋮⋮⋮∂2f∂xn∂x1∂2f∂xn∂x2⋯∂2f∂xn2].

In our case, we have

f″(x,y)=[∂2f∂x2∂2f∂x∂y∂2f∂y∂x∂2f∂y2].

First, notice that since f′(x,y)=[y−2xyx−x2], we must have

∂f∂x=y−2xy,∂f∂y=x−x2.

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

∂2f∂x2=∂∂x(y−2xy)=−2y∂2f∂x∂y=∂∂x(x−x2)=1−2x∂2f∂y∂x=∂∂y(y−2xy)=1−2x∂2f∂y2=∂∂y(x−x2)=0

So, the second derivative is

f″(x,y)=[−2y1−2x1−2x0].

Finally, we evaluate this matrix at (1,2). This gives

f″(1,2)=[−4−1−10].

q-163637.name: Question 4
q-163637.problem:
Find ${f}^{″}(\frac{1}{2},\frac{1}{2})$ for the function $f(x,y)$ given that
${f}^{′}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}10xy & 5{x}^{2}-2y\end{aligned}]$
q-163637.worked_solution:
For a function $f:{R}^{n}\to R,$ given by

$$
f:{{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}⟶f({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}),
$$

the second derivative of $f$ is given by the $n\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{″}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}^{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have

$$
{f}^{″}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

First, notice that since ${f}^{′}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}10xy & 5{x}^{2}-2y\end{aligned}],$ 
 we must have

$$
\frac{∂f}{∂x}=10xy,\,\frac{∂f}{∂y}=5{x}^{2}-2y.
$$

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(10xy)=10y\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(5{x}^{2}-2y)=10x \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(10xy)=10x\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(5{x}^{2}-2y)=-2\end{aligned}
$$

So, the second derivative is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}10y & 10x \\ 10x & -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate this matrix at $(\frac{1}{2},\frac{1}{2}).$ This gives

$$
{f}^{″}(\frac{1}{2},\frac{1}{2})=[\begin{aligned}5 & 5 \\ 5 & -2\end{aligned}].
$$

Find f″(12,12) for the function f(x,y) given that f′(x,y)=[10xy5x2−2y]

EXPLANATION

For a function f:Rn→R, given by f:[x1x2⋮xn]⏟x⟶f(x1,x2,…,xn),

the second derivative of f is given by the n×n matrix

f″(x)=[∂2f∂x12∂2f∂x1∂x2⋯∂2f∂x1∂xn∂2f∂x2∂x1∂2f∂x22⋯∂2f∂x2∂xn⋮⋮⋮⋮∂2f∂xn∂x1∂2f∂xn∂x2⋯∂2f∂xn2].

In our case, we have

f″(x,y)=[∂2f∂x2∂2f∂x∂y∂2f∂y∂x∂2f∂y2].

First, notice that since f′(x,y)=[10xy5x2−2y], we must have

∂f∂x=10xy,∂f∂y=5x2−2y.

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

∂2f∂x2=∂∂x(10xy)=10y∂2f∂x∂y=∂∂x(5x2−2y)=10x∂2f∂y∂x=∂∂y(10xy)=10x∂2f∂y2=∂∂y(5x2−2y)=−2

So, the second derivative is

f″(x,y)=[10y10x10x−2].

Finally, we evaluate this matrix at (12,12). This gives

f″(12,12)=[555−2].

q-81009.name: Question 5
q-81009.problem:
Find ${f}^{″}(x,y)$ for the function $f(x,y)$ given that
${f}^{′}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}-4y+1 & 3{y}^{2}-4x-1\end{aligned}]$
q-81009.worked_solution:
For a function $f:{R}^{n}\to R,$ given by

$$
f:{{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}⟶f({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}),
$$

the second derivative of $f$ is given by the $n\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{″}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}^{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have

$$
{f}^{″}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

First, notice that since ${f}^{′}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}-4y+1 & 3{y}^{2}-4x-1\end{aligned}],$ we must have

$$
\frac{∂f}{∂x}=-4y+1,\,\frac{∂f}{∂y}=3{y}^{2}-4x-1.
$$

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(-4y+1)=0\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(3{y}^{2}-4x-1)=-4 \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(-4y+1)=-4\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(3{y}^{2}-4x-1)=6y\end{aligned}
$$

So, the second derivative is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}0 & -4 \\ -4 & 6y\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

?

Find f″(x,y) for the function f(x,y) given that f′(x,y)=[−4y+13y2−4x−1]

a
[2x660]
b
[04x4x−4y]
c
[−2y4x4x0]
d
[0−4−46y]
e
[6y4x4x0]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

For a function f:Rn→R, given by f:[x1x2⋮xn]⏟x⟶f(x1,x2,…,xn),

the second derivative of f is given by the n×n matrix

f″(x)=[∂2f∂x12∂2f∂x1∂x2⋯∂2f∂x1∂xn∂2f∂x2∂x1∂2f∂x22⋯∂2f∂x2∂xn⋮⋮⋮⋮∂2f∂xn∂x1∂2f∂xn∂x2⋯∂2f∂xn2].

In our case, we have

f″(x,y)=[∂2f∂x2∂2f∂x∂y∂2f∂y∂x∂2f∂y2].

First, notice that since f′(x,y)=[−4y+13y2−4x−1], we must have

∂f∂x=−4y+1,∂f∂y=3y2−4x−1.

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

∂2f∂x2=∂∂x(−4y+1)=0∂2f∂x∂y=∂∂x(3y2−4x−1)=−4∂2f∂y∂x=∂∂y(−4y+1)=−4∂2f∂y2=∂∂y(3y2−4x−1)=6y

So, the second derivative is

f″(x,y)=[0−4−46y].

q-81033.name: Question 6
q-81033.worked_solution:
For a function $f:{R}^{n}\to R,$ given by

$$
f:{{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}⟶f({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}),
$$

the second derivative of $f$ is given by the $n\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{″}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}^{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have

$$
{f}^{″}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

First, we compute the first derivative of $f(x,y),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & \frac{∂f}{∂y}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡y) & \frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡y)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2x\operatorname{sin}⁡y & {x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡y\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2x\operatorname{sin}⁡y)=2\operatorname{sin}⁡y\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡y)=2x\operatorname{cos}⁡y \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(2x\operatorname{sin}⁡y)=2x\operatorname{cos}⁡y\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡y)=-{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡y\end{aligned}
$$

So, the second derivative is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}2\operatorname{sin}⁡y & 2x\operatorname{cos}⁡y \\ 2x\operatorname{cos}⁡y & -{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡y\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate this matrix at $(1,\pi ).$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(1,\pi )=[\begin{aligned}0 & -2 \\ -2 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

f″(x,y)=[∂2f∂x2∂2f∂x∂y∂2f∂y∂x∂2f∂y2].

f″(x,y)=[2sin⁡y2xcos⁡y2xcos⁡y−x2sin⁡y].

q-80939.worked_solution:
For a function $f:{R}^{n}\to R,$ given by

$$
f:{{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}⟶f({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}),
$$

the second derivative of $f$ is given by the $n\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{″}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}^{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have

$$
{f}^{″}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

First, we compute the first derivative of $f(x,y),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & \frac{∂f}{∂y}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}(x\operatorname{sin}⁡y+xy) & \frac{∂}{∂y}(x\operatorname{sin}⁡y+xy)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡y+y & x\operatorname{cos}⁡y+x\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{sin}⁡y+y)=0\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(x\operatorname{cos}⁡y+x)=\operatorname{cos}⁡y+1 \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{sin}⁡y+y)=\operatorname{cos}⁡y+1\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(x\operatorname{cos}⁡y+x)=-x\operatorname{sin}⁡y\end{aligned}
$$

So, the second derivative is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}0 & \operatorname{cos}⁡y+1 \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡y+1 & -x\operatorname{sin}⁡y\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

f″(x)=[∂2f∂x12∂2f∂x1∂x2⋯∂2f∂x1∂xn∂2f∂x2∂x1∂2f∂x22⋯∂2f∂x2∂xn⋮⋮⋮⋮∂2f∂xn∂x1∂2f∂xn∂x2⋯∂2f∂xn2].

In our case, we have

f″(x,y)=[∂2f∂x2∂2f∂x∂y∂2f∂y∂x∂2f∂y2].

First, we compute the first derivative of f(x,y), as follows:

f′(x,y)=[∂f∂x∂f∂y]=[∂∂x(xsin⁡y+xy)∂∂y(xsin⁡y+xy)]=[sin⁡y+yxcos⁡y+x]

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

f″(x,y)=[0cos⁡y+1cos⁡y+1−xsin⁡y].

q-80945.name: Question 8
q-80945.worked_solution:
For a function $f:{R}^{n}\to R,$ given by

$$
f:{{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}⟶f({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}),
$$

the second derivative of $f$ is given by the $n\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{″}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}^{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have

$$
{f}^{″}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

First, we compute the first derivative of $f(x,y),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & \frac{∂f}{∂y}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x-y)) & \frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x-y))\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x-y) & -\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x-y)\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x-y))=-4\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x-y)\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(-\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x-y))=2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x-y) \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x-y))=2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x-y)\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(-\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x-y))=-\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x-y)\end{aligned}
$$

So, the second derivative is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}-4\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x-y) & 2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x-y) \\ 2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x-y) & -\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x-y)\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate this matrix at $(0,-\frac{\pi }{2}).$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(0,-\frac{\pi }{2})=[\begin{aligned}-4 & 2 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$
{f}^{″}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}^{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have

$$
{f}^{″}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

First, we compute the first derivative of $f(x,y),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & \frac{∂f}{∂y}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}((y-1)({x}^{2}-1)) & \frac{∂}{∂y}((y-1)({x}^{2}-1))\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2x(y-1) & {x}^{2}-1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2x(y-1))=2(y-1)\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}-1)=2x \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(2x(y-1))=2x\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}-1)=0\end{aligned}
$$

So, the second derivative is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}2(y-1) & 2x \\ 2x & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate this matrix at $(-1,2).$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(-1,2)=[\begin{aligned}2 & -2 \\ -2 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

f″(x)=[∂2f∂x12∂2f∂x1∂x2⋯∂2f∂x1∂xn∂2f∂x2∂x1∂2f∂x22⋯∂2f∂x2∂xn⋮⋮⋮⋮∂2f∂xn∂x1∂2f∂xn∂x2⋯∂2f∂xn2].

f″(x,y)=[∂2f∂x2∂2f∂x∂y∂2f∂y∂x∂2f∂y2].

f′(x,y)=[∂f∂x∂f∂y]=[∂∂x((y−1)(x2−1))∂∂y((y−1)(x2−1))]=[2x(y−1)x2−1]

∂2f∂x2=∂∂x(2x(y−1))=2(y−1)∂2f∂x∂y=∂∂x(x2−1)=2x∂2f∂y∂x=∂∂y(2x(y−1))=2x∂2f∂y2=∂∂y(x2−1)=0

So, the second derivative is

f″(x,y)=[2(y−1)2x2x0].

Finally, we evaluate this matrix at (−1,2). This gives

f″(−1,2)=[2−2−20].

q-80943.name: Question 10
q-80943.worked_solution:
For a function $f:{R}^{n}\to R,$ given by

$$
f:{{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}⟶f({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}),
$$

the second derivative of $f$ is given by the $n\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{″}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}^{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have

$$
{f}^{″}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

First, we compute the first derivative of $f(x,y),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & \frac{∂f}{∂y}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}({e}^{x}\operatorname{sin}⁡y) & \frac{∂}{∂y}({e}^{x}\operatorname{sin}⁡y)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{e}^{x}\operatorname{sin}⁡y & {e}^{x}\operatorname{cos}⁡y\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({e}^{x}\operatorname{sin}⁡y)={e}^{x}\operatorname{sin}⁡y\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({e}^{x}\operatorname{cos}⁡y)={e}^{x}\operatorname{cos}⁡y \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({e}^{x}\operatorname{sin}⁡y)={e}^{x}\operatorname{cos}⁡y\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({e}^{x}\operatorname{cos}⁡y)=-{e}^{x}\operatorname{sin}⁡y\end{aligned}
$$

So, the second derivative is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}{e}^{x}\operatorname{sin}⁡y & {e}^{x}\operatorname{cos}⁡y \\ {e}^{x}\operatorname{cos}⁡y & -{e}^{x}\operatorname{sin}⁡y\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

q-80943.html:
Question 10
?

Find f″(x,y) for the function f(x,y)=exsin⁡y.

a
 [excos⁡y−exsin⁡yexsin⁡yexcos⁡y]
b
 [exsin⁡ycos⁡ycos⁡y−exsin⁡y]
c
[−excos⁡yexsin⁡yexsin⁡yexcos⁡y]
d
[excos⁡yexsin⁡y−exsin⁡yexcos⁡y]
e
[exsin⁡yexcos⁡yexcos⁡y−exsin⁡y]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

For a function f:Rn→R, given by f:[x1x2⋮xn]⏟x⟶f(x1,x2,…,xn),

the second derivative of f is given by the n×n matrix

f″(x)=[∂2f∂x12∂2f∂x1∂x2⋯∂2f∂x1∂xn∂2f∂x2∂x1∂2f∂x22⋯∂2f∂x2∂xn⋮⋮⋮⋮∂2f∂xn∂x1∂2f∂xn∂x2⋯∂2f∂xn2].

In our case, we have

f″(x,y)=[∂2f∂x2∂2f∂x∂y∂2f∂y∂x∂2f∂y2].

First, we compute the first derivative of f(x,y), as follows:

f′(x,y)=[∂f∂x∂f∂y]=[∂∂x(exsin⁡y)∂∂y(exsin⁡y)]=[exsin⁡yexcos⁡y]

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

∂2f∂x2=∂∂x(exsin⁡y)=exsin⁡y∂2f∂x∂y=∂∂x(excos⁡y)=excos⁡y∂2f∂y∂x=∂∂y(exsin⁡y)=excos⁡y∂2f∂y2=∂∂y(excos⁡y)=−exsin⁡y

So, the second derivative is

f″(x,y)=[exsin⁡yexcos⁡yexcos⁡y−exsin⁡y].

${f}^{′}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}2(x-1){y}^{2} & 2(x-1)^{2}y\end{aligned}],$ 
evaluate the Hessian determinant of $f(x,y)$ at the point $(0,1).$
q-81023.worked_solution:
For a function $f:{R}^{n}\to R,$ given by

$$
f:{{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}⟶f({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}),
$$

the second derivative of $f$ is given by the $n\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{″}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}^{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

The Hessian determinant $H(x,y)$ is the determinant of the second derivative:

$$
H(x)=det({f}^{″}(x))
$$

In our case, we have

$$
{f}^{″}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

First, notice that since ${f}^{′}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}2(x-1){y}^{2} & 2(x-1)^{2}y\end{aligned}],$ we must have

$$
\frac{∂f}{∂x}=2(x-1){y}^{2},\,\frac{∂f}{∂y}=2(x-1)^{2}y.
$$

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2(x-1){y}^{2})=2{y}^{2}\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2(x-1)^{2}y)=4(x-1)y \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(2(x-1){y}^{2})=4(x-1)y\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(2(x-1)^{2}y)=2(x-1)^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the second derivative is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2{y}^{2} & 4(x-1)y \\ 4(x-1)y & 2(x-1)^{2}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

 

Evaluating the second derivative at $(0,1),$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(0,1)=[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 \\ -4 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we have

$$
H(0,1)=2\cdot 2-(-4)\cdot (-4)=-12.
$$

$$

$$

$$

$$
\frac{∂f}{∂x}=2x{y}^{2},\,\frac{∂f}{∂y}=2y{x}^{2}-1.

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2x{y}^{2})=2{y}^{2}\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2y{x}^{2}-1)=4xy \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(2x{y}^{2})=4xy\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(2y{x}^{2}-1)=2{x}^{2}\end{aligned}
